name: LGD-3303
lead: LGD-3303 is an investigational, orally available nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator developed by Ligand Pharmaceuticals, with a tricyclic pyrrolo[3,2-f]quinolin-7-one structure [1][2]. Published work consists of animal and in vitro studies of its pharmacokinetics, muscle and bone effects and effects on sexual behaviour in female rats [2][3][4].
No registered human trial was found, and it is not approved for any use [1]. SARMs are prohibited in sport, and detection studies of LGD-3303 metabolites in horses have been published [1][5].

paras: In castrated male rats, LGD-3303 showed potent activity on the levator ani muscle with partial agonist activity on the prostate; prostate weight remained at or below intact-animal levels as plasma concentrations rose [1][2]. Authors of the 2009 study interpreted tissue selectivity as arising from receptor-level interactions rather than differences in distribution [1][2].

No studies found in humans. Published work is limited to animals: in ovariectomized female rats, LGD-3303 increased muscle weight and bone mineral density and combined additively with a bisphosphonate [3]; in female rats it increased male-directed sexual preference in sexually experienced animals [4]. A ClinicalTrials.gov search returned no records for it [1].

No human safety data were identified. The FDA states that SARMs are unapproved and cannot be legally marketed as supplements or drugs, and has reported liver injury and cardiovascular events for the class [1]. Studies of horses describe the compound as prohibited in equine and human sport and propose a metabolite as a doping-control target [1][5].

timeline.event: Pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic and bone-combination studies in rats published [2][3]
Study of effects on female rat sexual behaviour published [4]
Equine in vivo metabolite profiling for doping control published [5]

card.summary: A Ligand Pharmaceuticals nonsteroidal SARM tested only in rats and horses; no human data.
card.note: Preclinical only; banned in sport; unapproved.

quick.overview:
LGD-3303 is an experimental SARM made by Ligand Pharmaceuticals. Animal studies looked at its effects on muscle, bone and female sexual behaviour.

No human trial has been registered, so its effects in people are unknown.
quick.mechanism: It activates the androgen receptor; in rats it stimulated muscle strongly while only partially stimulating prostate tissue.
quick.risks: There are no human safety data. SARMs as a class are unapproved, banned in sport, and linked in reports to liver injury.
